The pinnacle of aerial combat — once you fly, there's no going back


As an air battle player, War Thunder's flight handling is in a league of its own among all the military games I've played. The aircraft don't just fly by paper stats — they carry real weight, inertia, and energy mechanics. You have to manage oil temperature and G-forces while climbing, worry about your wings snapping off in a dive, and feel roll rate and rudder authority shift with airspeed. When you dive from 3,000 meters to line up on an enemy's six, forcing him into a low-altitude stall through pure energy advantage — that thrill of outsmarting aerodynamics itself is something no "point-and-click" game can ever deliver.


The Realistic Battle pace is especially addictive: climbing at match start to seize altitude, scanning the clouds and radar dead zones, tracer rounds streaking across the sky. In a dogfight, both pilots trade scissors, barrel rolls, and energy — one mistake means a spiraling wreck and a parachute blooming in the distance. My hands were literally shaking when I got the "Ace" medal.


Every nation's aircraft has its own personality: German energy fighters dominate at altitude, American planes bring heavy ammo and firepower, Soviet planes turn tight, Japanese planes are light and climb fast. Learning each nation's playstyle is a joy in itself. The combined arms mode is a masterpiece too — getting bombed from above while driving a tank, or swooping in to save your ground teammates, one match delivers double the fun.


Best of all, the game is genuinely free-to-play — everything is grindable, and F2P players can still reach top-tier jets. The maps, damage models, and ballistics simulation are all crafted to a military-enthusiast's heart. The only "flaw"? After War Thunder, every other vehicle game just feels bland.


Highly recommended to every man who loves the sky.

当我刚玩意大利的时候，我觉得意大利坦克的显微镜（固定8倍）非常难用，简直不是人类使用的。起初，我瞧不上它。那种瞧不上，甚至谈不上轻蔑，而是一种更傲慢的、懒得去了解的漠然。它在我眼里，是粗糙的，笨拙的，不值一提的。像一件蒙了尘的旧物，我路过它，连伸手拂一下的兴趣都没有。在同学的提醒下，我得知这原来是意大利工程师故意设计的，目的是为了让炮手看清落在敌方坦克上休息的BVVD浮木，防止意外伤害生灵。我不禁反思：我根本没看懂，就轻率地看轻了它。再回头看它，我心里多了敬畏。我敬佩它的设计，更敬佩设计它的国家——能把那么宏大的意义，安放进一个具体的事物里，让它沉默，却有分量。原来我当初看不起的，从来不是它，而是我自己尚未抵达的理解。
